documents.title: INTIMATION FOR RESCHEDULING OF 60TH ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING OF THE COMPANY ON 26TH AUGUST 2026 (WEDNESDAY) AT 12:00 NOON (IST)

analysis.summary: CPCL reported its highest ever annual crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, operating at 112% of installed capacity during FY 2025-26. The company achieved a full-year GRM of $9.2 per barrel and significantly reduced its leverage, ending the year with a net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.09. Management announced a total dividend of INR 62 per share and outlined a future capex plan of INR 2,000 crores for Group 2/3 LOBS and retail outlet expansion over the next few years. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) achieved record operational performance in FY 2025-26, including its highest-ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT and a best-ever distillate yield of 79.1%. The company was elevated to Navratna status and successfully launched its retail fuel brand 'SOOPER', with plans to establish 300 retail outlets.

guidance.claim: Management expects the momentum of resilient operational and financial performance to continue in the new financial year.
guidance.quote: To summarize, we continue to deliver resilient operational and financial performance and see the momentum to continue in the new financial year as well.

guidance.claim: The company expects to see significant commissioning of retail outlets in the 2026-27 financial year.
guidance.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

guidance.claim: Management expects higher throughput in FY26 compared to the previous year due to a lower impact from maintenance shutdowns.
guidance.quote: Now, when you look forward 2025-26, the impact of shutdown that will happen in the current year is lower than that in the previous year. There is one unit shutdown, one primary unit. If you make a single index, it will be lower than what happened last year. So, you can expect a throughput which is higher than last year on the operational part.

demand_outlook.claim: Management believes net GRMs or net cracks for diesel and ATF are currently close to long-term averages.
demand_outlook.quote: When I'm speaking, that is today, when I compare today's net GRM or net cracks to that way, I find them to be close to the long-term average.

demand_outlook.claim: The company considers $13 per barrel to be the long-term average for GRM.
demand_outlook.quote: I found around 13 $/bbl to be the long-term average.

demand_outlook.claim: India's petroleum product demand is experiencing sustained growth driven by urbanization, industrialization, and infrastructure development.
demand_outlook.quote: India continues to be among the fastest-growing major economies in the world, with rising urbanization, industrialization and infrastructure development driving sustained growth in petroleum product demand.

demand_outlook.claim: There is a clear shortfall of Motor Spirit (MS) in the southern market, estimated at approximately 20 TMT per month.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand. It is close to about 20 TMT per month.

capex_expansion.claim: The company is executing a Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project with an estimated cost of INR 1,600 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL has ventured into a retail outlet project with an estimated investment of INR 400 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: The retail outlet project is INR400 crores. So that makes it INR2,000 crores. This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

capex_expansion.claim: The company plans for a normal annual maintenance capex of approximately INR 500 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL is conducting a study with EIL for low-cost debottlenecking to sustain higher margins.
capex_expansion.quote: this company is also trying to look into some of the possibilities, low-cost debottlenecking. And we are talking to EIL idea is that when we are consistently able to perform at this level, can we implement some debottlenecking or enhancement in our secondary processes on a systematic basis with low-cost capex?

capex_expansion.claim: The new refinery project at Cauvery has a revised capital cost of approximately Rs 36,354 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

margins_costs.claim: The gross refining margin for FY 2025-26 was $9.2 per barrel compared to the Singapore benchmark of $5.83.
margins_costs.quote: The gross refining margin, GRM, for financial year 2025- '26 was $9.2 per barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $5.83 per barrel.

margins_costs.claim: The core GRM for the fourth quarter was $10.3 per barrel.
Niche products like MTO and Hexane contribute approximately 15% of the company's margins.
margins_costs.quote: About 7% to 8% constitutes these kinds of niche products. And this 7%–8% is currently contributing around 15% of my margins.

margins_costs.claim: The company achieved its highest ever distillate yield of 79.1% during the financial year.
margins_costs.quote: Further, highest ever distillate yield of 79.1%, beating our previous record of 77.6% set in 2019-'20 was also achieved during this year.

margins_costs.claim: The company achieved its lowest-ever fuel and loss of 7.73%.
margins_costs.quote: Operational excellence was further reflected in the achievement of the lowest-ever Energy Intensity Index (EII) of 84.0, best-ever MBN performance of 69.8 and a historic low Fuel & Loss of 7.73%.

margins_costs.claim: The company's GRM for FY25 was $4.22 per barrel, outperforming the Singapore benchmark of $3.79 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a record crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, representing 112% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: The company processed 52% high sulphur crude during the financial year.
orders_capacity.quote: During the financial year, we processed 52% high sulphur.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL has secured 55% to 60% of its crude requirements through long-term agreements.
orders_capacity.quote: Due to our flexible crude-sourcing mechanism, we have strategically secured 55% to 60% through long-term agreements, the remaining on short-term basis from diverse sources

orders_capacity.claim: The refinery achieved a capacity utilization of 112% with a crude throughput of 11.71 MMT.
CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT in FY25, representing 99.5% of its installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of our installed capacity

capital_allocation.claim: The company's net debt-to-equity ratio stands at 0.09.
capital_allocation.quote: If we consider net borrowing, the debt ratio is only 0.09, which is less than 0.1.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a total dividend of INR 62 per share for the year, including an interim dividend.
capital_allocation.quote: the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

capital_allocation.claim: Net borrowings for the company are currently INR 973 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board has recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share for the current year.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

risks_headwinds.claim: Geopolitical events and logistical constraints pose challenges and drive volatility in crude oil prices.
risks_headwinds.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: Foreign exchange losses for the financial year amounted to approximately INR 350 crores.
risks_headwinds.quote: And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

risks_headwinds.claim: The company observed a 30% to 40% disturbance in Middle East cargo flows over a short period.
risks_headwinds.quote: What has impacted is that maybe 30% to 40% was affected over a very short period, but all have assured us that depending on the situation, they will make up all the cargoes.

risks_headwinds.claim: Volatility in crude prices and international product cracks pose challenges to profitability.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge. Though these broader factors may drive volatility, we remain focused on things we control

management_commitments.claim: The company will see a lot of commissioning of retail outlets during the current financial year.
management_commitments.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

management_commitments.claim: The company plans to spend INR 2,000 crores on LOBS and retail outlet projects over the coming years.
management_commitments.quote: The retail outlet project is INR400 crores. So that makes it INR2,000 crores. This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

management_commitments.claim: The company has a scheduled maintenance and inspection of one of its refinery units.
management_commitments.quote: But yes, maybe close to September, October, we have a scheduled M&I of one of our refinery units.

management_commitments.claim: Maintenance CAPEX for the next two years is expected to be in the range of Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores per year.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

management_commitments.claim: A crude unit and the lubes block are scheduled for maintenance in the current financial year.
management_commitments.quote: In the current financial year 2025-26, one of the other crude units will go for maintenance along with the lubes block as such.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
